headline: Riots reignite French debt rout as Macron struggles to restore order
deck: Gap with German borrowing costs widens to 150 basis points as curfews imposed in Paris, Lille and Nice
body: Investors dumped French government bonds yesterday as violent protests spread across the country, pushing the gap between French and German borrowing costs to its widest level since the eurozone debt crisis. The spread between ten-year French and German yields rose to about 150 basis points, according to traders, as the government imposed overnight curfews in Paris, Lille and Nice after a weekend of rioting and looting. Analysts said the unrest had made it harder for the prime minister to pass a budget that would reassure markets about the trajectory of public debt, which is forecast to keep rising next year. Officials insisted that public finances remained under control and that spending plans would be presented to parliament as scheduled, despite calls from opposition parties to delay the vote. Bank shares also fell sharply, with the largest lenders losing between four and six per cent, while the euro weakened against the dollar and sterling in afternoon trading in London.
other_text: Chancellor rules out capital gains tax rise The chancellor has ruled out raising capital gains tax in next month's Budget, easing concerns among entrepreneurs and investors who had warned that a sharp increase would drive capital overseas. Treasury officials are instead examining changes to pension tax relief and property levies to close a shortfall in the public finances.
